Definition: probably from G4862; common, i.e. (literally) shared by all or several, or (ceremonially) profane:--common, defiled, unclean, unholy.
KeyPassages: Mark 7:2; Acts 2:44; Romans 14:14; Titus 1:4; Hebrews 10:29; Jude 1:3
BiblicalUsage: Koinos means common, shared by all, and so, in the ceremonial sense, profane. Mark 7:2 faults the disciples for eating with defiled, unwashen hands, Acts 2:44 says all that believed were together and had all things common, Romans 14:14 says there is nothing unclean of itself, but to him that esteemeth any thing to be unclean, to him it is unclean, Titus 1:4 greets Titus in the common faith, Hebrews 10:29 warns of counting the blood of the covenant an unholy thing, and Jude 1:3 writes of the common salvation.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe koinos holds the whole argument of the church: what is common is shared, and what is shared is holy. I hold that the common faith and the common salvation are the same gift, and the blood no one may call common is the blood that makes all things common.
RelatedBooks: Mark; Acts; Romans; Titus; Hebrews; Jude
